episode_title: He Sold His Car to Buy His First Property: Now He Owns 40 Rentals!

real_qa.q: How did Lawrence Gerges get his first down payment for real estate investing as a college student with no W-2 income?
real_qa.r: He sold his car for around $16,000. He used a family hand-me-down car from 2008 instead. With this money and additional scrounged savings, he put together enough for a down payment on his first property in Peoria, Illinois, where he put down $15,300 on a $65,000 purchase price.
real_qa.requete: Lawrence Gerges first down payment sold car

real_qa.q: What financing method did Landlord Larry use to buy his first rental property without W-2 income or pay stubs?
real_qa.r: He applied for a DSCR (Debt Service Coverage Ratio) loan because he had no W-2 income, no pay stubs, and no traditional income documentation. He found the lender through BiggerPockets by searching for someone offering sub-100K loan amounts with DSCR financing.
real_qa.requete: DSCR loan no W-2 income first rental property

real_qa.q: How much monthly cash flow did Landlord Larry generate from his first Section 8 property in Peoria, Illinois?
real_qa.r: He received $1,400 in rent from a Section 8 tenant whose income was zero, so the government paid 100% of the rent. His mortgage payment was $480, leaving him with approximately $600 to $700 per month in net cash flow after accounting for basic expenses.
real_qa.requete: Landlord Larry first property cash flow $1400

real_qa.q: What strategy did Landlord Larry use to find his first investment property in Cleveland, Ohio after moving from California?
real_qa.r: Before moving, he called listing agents and requested video tours and answered questions about neighborhoods, researching about 50 agents' listings remotely. Once he arrived in Cleveland at the end of July 2024, he toured over 60-70 properties in his first week with a local agent, creating a 50-60 house list to understand which areas were good or bad to invest in.
real_qa.requete: Landlord Larry Cleveland Ohio research video tours strategy

real_qa.q: How did Landlord Larry identify rent increase opportunities in Section 8 properties that previous landlords had missed?
real_qa.r: He discovered that his first Cleveland duplex was a three-bedroom but had only two-bedroom Section 8 vouchers, meaning it could be rented at the higher two-bedroom rate of around $1,200 instead of the $650 it was getting. Previous owners had not submitted rent increase requests to the housing authority, possibly because they lacked local agents or simply did not think about it. Within three months, both units increased to the $1,200 two-bedroom standard rent.
real_qa.requete: Section 8 rent increase opportunity three bedroom two bedroom voucher

real_qa.q: What was the purchase price and cash flow of Landlord Larry's first Cleveland duplex deal?
real_qa.r: He purchased the duplex for $88,000 with a mortgage payment of exactly $675. With two Section 8 tenants paying $650 each (before increases), water and sewer costs were minimal, and he was making approximately $500-600 net monthly cash flow. After three months, the rents increased to $1,200 each, significantly increasing cash flow.

guest.bio_context: Lawrence Gerges, known as Landlord Larry on Instagram and TikTok, started investing in Section 8 real estate during his junior year in college in Southern California. After a conversation with a regretful investment banker at a pizza parlor changed his trajectory away from finance, he sold his car for $16,000 to fund his first down payment. He has been actively investing for a little over three years and has built a portfolio of 40 rental properties, primarily in Cleveland, Ohio.
